answer: An agent market can require each participant to lock a scarce token deposit before earning fees, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove coordinated duplicate identities claimed the same work. Creating extra names is easy; making each one eligible ties influence to capital that cannot be reused across simultaneous claims. A summit of auditors can publish the evidence, while copper and canyon label two test agents whose deposits are at risk. The attacker pays for every identity and loses stake when caught.
